A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf V$ be the [[Definition:Variety (Universal Algebra)|variety]] defined by a set $E$ of identities, and $X$ a set.
Then $\map {F_{\mathbf V} } X = \map T X / \approx_E$, where $s \approx_E t$ {{iff}} $E \models s = t$, is [[Definition:Free Algebra|free]] in $\mathbf V$ on $X$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\theta$ be a [[Definition:Congruence Relation|congruence]] on an algebra $A$ and $h: A \to B$ a [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphism]] with $\theta \subseteq \map \ker h$.
Then $h$ factors uniquely through $A / \theta$.

derived.the factorization: the universal property of the free algebra

object_map.reformulation: Collapse the absolutely free term algebra by everything the identities force, and check that every evaluation into V kills it.

validity_conditions: Equational consequence is a congruence closed under substitution, so the quotient again satisfies E.
Every algebra in V satisfies E, which puts the congruence inside the kernel of each evaluation.
proof_plan: The term algebra $\map T X$ is absolutely free: every map $X \to A$ extends uniquely to a homomorphism $h: \map T X \to A$, by evaluation.
$\approx_E$ is a congruence, and $\map T X / \approx_E$ satisfies every identity of $E$, so it lies in $\mathbf V$.
If $A \in \mathbf V$ then $A$ satisfies $E$, so $s \approx_E t$ implies $\map h s = \map h t$; that is, $\approx_E \subseteq \map \ker h$.
